issue: 'lancheira' in pt-BR denotes the container (a child's lunchbox/bag), not the boxed meal itself. It is effectively the gloss of 弁当箱, not 弁当, and teaches the learner the wrong referent. 'marmita' and 'bentô' already cover the sense correctly.

current: to fit, to suit, to match
fix: Remove sense 2 entirely (en 'to fit, to suit, to match'; pt 'combinar, cair bem, ajustar-se'). Leave only sense 1 'to meet, to see (someone)' / 'encontrar, encontrar-se com, ver (alguém)'. The fit/suit/match meaning belongs to the separate verb 合う.
issue: Sense belongs to the homophone 合う (JMdict 1284430), not 会う (1198180), whose only JMdict senses are 'to meet/encounter/see' and 'to have an accident/bad experience' (esp. 遭う). Remove the whole sense, incl. pt 'combinar, cair bem, ajustar-se'.

fix: Remove sense 2 (en 'uncle (formal/written)'; pt 'tio'). Keep only sense 1 'count (nobleman), earl' / 'conde'. If desired, the standalone word's other real senses are (hist) chief of a bureau and abbr. for Brazil — but never 'uncle'.
issue: Standalone 伯(はく) has no 'uncle' sense; JMdict 1474240 senses are count/earl, ritsuryō chief official (hist), Brazil (abbr). 'Uncle' is the word 伯父(おじ) / the kanji's role in compounds. Remove the sense, incl. pt 'tio'.

fix: Remove sense 2 (en 'rank, degree, grade'; pt 'posição, grau'). Keep only the particle/suffix sense 'approximately, about, to the extent of'. The noun meaning 'rank/grade' belongs to the separate 位 (くらい) noun entry, not this suf/prt entry.
issue: 'Rank/degree/grade' is the separate noun lexeme 位(くらい) (JMdict 1154330), not this suf/prt entry (1154340: approximately; to the extent that; as...as). Gloss also contradicts the sense's suf/prt pos. Remove the sense, incl. pt 'posição, grau'.

fix: Replace sense 2. pos: change [pn] to [pref]. en: ['how many, how much (prefix before a counter, e.g. 何人, 何時, 何歳)']. pt: ['quantos, quantas; quanto (prefixo antes de um contador)']. Remove the 'how (exclamatory)' / 'como (exclamação)' gloss.
issue: 何(なん) has no exclamatory 'how' sense — that is 何と/なんて (separate entries). JMdict 2846738 sense 2 is the must-know prefix 'how many' before a counter (何時, 何人, 何歳), which is missing. Replace en and pt (pt → 'quantos, quantas (antes de contador)').

fix: Split the single element into two array items: ["umbrella", "parasol"] to match the one-gloss-per-element convention used by every other entry (and by this entry's own pt field ["guarda-chuva","sombrinha"]).
issue: Two EN glosses are joined into a single array element with a comma, unlike every other entry in the batch which stores one gloss per element. Content itself is correct (kasa = umbrella; parasol).

Gloss 'aquilo' belongs to あれ (distal demonstrative), not それ. The EN gloss itself specifies '(near the listener)', which maps to isso/esse in pt-BR; aquilo/aquele maps to あれ. Including 'aquilo' breaks the ko-so-a-do correspondence the course must teach and conflates two contrasting words.

'a frente' (article + noun, 'the front') is a crase/spelling error for the adverbial meaning 'in front' that it is meant to render (EN 'in front'); as written it is redundant with 'frente'. Should be 'à frente' or 'na frente'.

fix: Remove the second sense entirely. Keep only sense 1: en "uncle (younger than parent)" / pt "tio (mais novo que o pai/mãe)". The kanji 叔父 (reading おじ) denotes a blood-relative uncle only; the 'middle-aged man / mister' meaning is a distinct homophonous lexeme written 小父(さん) / おじさん and must not be taught under 叔父. The sense label itself ('as おじさん') shows it does not apply to the bare おじ headword.
issue: The 'middle-aged man' sense belongs to the homophone lexeme 小父 (おじさん), not to 叔父. JMdict 1607070 (叔父/伯父) means only 'uncle'. Attaching this sense to hw 叔父 teaches false kanji usage; the pt glosses 'senhor, tio (homem de meia-idade)' inherit the same error.

fix: pt: ["movimento"] — drop "moção". In pt-BR "moção" means almost exclusively a formal/parliamentary motion (moção de repúdio/apoio); the physical-movement sense is archaic and not what a learner infers. "movimento" already covers both en glosses 'motion' and 'movement'.
issue: 'moção' in Brazilian Portuguese means almost exclusively a formal/parliamentary motion (moção de repúdio); as a gloss for physical motion it is a misleading calque of English 'motion'. Drop it — 'movimento' already covers the sense.

fix: Retag senses[1].pos from ['adv'] to ['adj-na'] and keep the glosses 'awful; tough; a big deal (situation)' — they are the na-adjective sense. Also consider adding 'adj-na' to senses[0].pos, since 大変 is both adj-na and adv in JMdict (the adverb sense 'very/terribly' and the na-adjective sense 'tough/serious' coexist).
issue: Sense pos is adv, but glosses are adjectival/nominal ('awful, tough, a big deal') — these belong to the adj-na sense of 大変 (serious; hard; tough). As an adverb 大変 only means 'very/terribly', which sense 0 already covers. Mislabeled sense can teach wrong usage.

fix: Drop 'gostado'; ['gostar de', 'preferido'] already cover 好き. If an adjectival 'liked/beloved' gloss is desired, use 'querido' or 'predileto/favorito' rather than 'gostado'.
issue: 'gostado' is not used as a standalone adjective in Brazilian Portuguese (gostar is only 'gostar de'; passive/adjectival 'gostado' is unnatural). Reads as a translation artifact of 'liked'.

fix: Split the comma-packed element into two: ['student', 'pupil'] — one gloss per element, matching the rest of the corpus and mirroring the two-element pt array. (The 'esp. university student' nuance is optional and secondary; the packing is the actual defect.)
issue: Two glosses packed into one array element ('student, pupil') — every other entry stores one gloss per element. Also 'pupil' better matches 生徒/児童; 学生 is a student, esp. university student.

The sense 'to sting, to bite (insect)' belongs to the homophone 刺す (JMdict 1315520), not 差す. 差す (1291330) means to shine (light), to hold up (an umbrella), to insert/pour — never to sting. Teaches a wrong kanji-meaning pairing.
pt glosses 'picar, ferroar' render the sting/bite sense of the homophone 刺す, which is not a meaning of 差す. Must be replaced together with the EN gloss of this sense.

fix: aquela pessoa; aquele (pessoa distante de ambos)
issue: Glosses belong to the homophone 彼(かれ) 'he' (JMdict 1483150). This record's kana is あれ: 彼(あれ) is the distal demonstrative 'that / that thing'. As written the entry teaches the wrong lexeme; likely a mislinked entry.

fix: aquela pessoa; aquele (pessoa distante de ambos)
issue: pt mirrors the かれ mix-up: 彼(あれ) does not mean 'ele'; it is the demonstrative 'aquilo/aquele'.

fix: aquela pessoa; aquele (pessoa distante de ambos)
issue: 'boyfriend' is sense 2 of 彼(かれ), not of 彼(あれ). あれ's secondary personal use is 'that person (distant from both speaker and listener)'.

fix: aquela pessoa; aquele (pessoa distante de ambos)
issue: 'namorado' renders the かれ 'boyfriend' gloss; wrong lexeme for 彼(あれ).

fix: Relink to the intended common homophone 石鹸(せっけん) 'soap' (pt: sabão/sabonete) and set level by the ≥3-list consensus rule, or drop 接見 from N5. 接見 is an advanced formal/legal term ('interview; audience; lawyer's visit to a detainee') absent from N5 lists.
issue: 接見 ('audience; legal visit to a detainee') is an advanced formal/legal word, absent from N5 lists. The actual N5 word read せっけん is 石鹸 'soap' — this looks like a homophone mislink. Glosses are correct for 接見, but the item does not belong in an N5 course.

fix: Remove 'aquilo (ali, longe de ambos)'; keep 'aquele' and 'aquela' (aquele/aquela + substantivo, longe de ambos).
issue: 'aquilo' is a standalone neuter pronoun (= あれ) and can never modify a noun, while あの (adj-pn) is strictly prenominal. Listing it conflates あの with あれ — a core N5 distinction the course must keep clean.

fix: Remove 'portão' (= 門); keep 'porta (de correr)'; optionally add 'veneziana/postigo' (shutter).
issue: 戸(と) is a door / sliding panel (incl. shutters); a gate is 門. JMdict 1266970 lists no 'gate' sense, so 'gate' teaches a wrong equivalence.

fix: Remove 'portão' (= 門); keep 'porta (de correr)'; optionally add 'veneziana/postigo' (shutter).
issue: 'portão' = 門, aligned with the incorrect en gloss 'gate'. Also 'porta (de correr)' over-narrows — 戸 is any door, especially sliding.

fix: pt: ["hora (sufixo)", "...horas (ao indicar o horário: 3時 = três horas)"]
issue: 'em ponto' means 'sharp / exactly on the hour' (Japanese ちょうど), a nuance the suffix 時 does not carry; 時 attaches even to non-exact times (3時15分). Learner may think 3時 means '3 em ponto'.

"abafado" means muggy/stuffy (humid, poorly ventilated) — the standard pt-BR equivalent of 蒸し暑い, not plain 暑い. It is absent from the EN gloss "hot (weather, air)" and blurs the distinction with mushiatsui.

fix: pt: ["cálice de saquê", "taça para bebidas alcoólicas"]
issue: 杯 read さかずき means specifically a sake cup (small cup for alcoholic drinks), not a generic cup/glass. Leading glosses 'cup' and 'glass' belong to コップ/カップ or the counter 杯(はい); they teach the learner that さかずき is the everyday word for any cup or glass, which is false.

fix: pt: ["cálice de saquê", "taça para bebidas alcoólicas"]
issue: Mirrors the EN defect: 'copo' and 'taça' are generic drinking-vessel words (コップ/カップ), wrong for さかずき, which is specifically the small cup used for saquê. Only 'cálice (de saquê)' is correct.

current: to keep (a diary, records); to make an entry
issue: This sense belongs to the homophone 付ける (to write down; to keep a diary/records), not 点ける. 点ける only means to turn on / light (fire, candle, cigarette); 日記を点ける is incorrect kanji usage, so the entry teaches a false meaning.
Mirrors the homophone error in the EN gloss: 'manter (um diário)' renders a sense of 付ける, not 点ける. The second sense of 点ける is lighting/igniting, not record-keeping.
'roupa para lavar' denotes the laundry items, which is 洗濯物, not 洗濯. 洗濯 refers only to the act of washing; this gloss teaches a wrong noun referent (learner may say 洗濯を畳む instead of 洗濯物を畳む).

current: to become, to turn into, to come to be
issue: 生る(なる) means 'to bear fruit' (of plants, JMdict 1611000). The glosses given belong to the homophone 成る/為る 'to become' (JMdict 1375610). The entry teaches a false meaning for this exact hw+kana pair.
pt mirrors the homophone's meaning: 生る means 'dar fruto' (planta que produz fruto), not 'tornar-se/virar' (that is 成る). Sense-changing mistranslation.

'assunto' (topic/subject under discussion) is not a meaning of 物; that is 事/話題. The abstract sense of もの is 'things (in general/situation)', already covered by 'as coisas (situação)'. A learner would wrongly use 物 for 'assunto'.

Gloss belongs to the homophone 達 (tachi, JMdict 1416220), the pluralizing suffix. This entry (1551240, 立ち) means departure/setting off, being used up, rehearsal, etc. — never a plural suffix. If the plural suffix was intended (it is the N5 word), the record should be re-keyed to 達.
Faithful translation of the wrong English gloss: 立ち is not the plural suffix (that is 達). Must be fixed together with senses[0].en; the plural-suffix meaning teaches a false kanji-word association.

"To pass (of time)" is the meaning of the homophone verb 経つ (たつ), a separate lexeme. JMdict 1597040 立つ has no time-elapse sense; writing 時間が立つ is nonstandard. Replace with a genuine 立つ sense (e.g. to depart/leave, JMdict senses 4-5) or delete the sense.
Renders the 経つ meaning ("passar (tempo); decorrer"), which does not belong to 立つ. Must be fixed together with senses[2].en to whatever genuine 立つ sense replaces it.

EN sense is the belittling "the likes of" (JMdict: lessening the significance of the previous word), but the pt renders the neutral "things/something like" — duplicating sense 1 and losing the derogatory/humbling nuance that is the whole point of this sense.

fix: Remove senses[0] ('to take (time)', 'to cost (money)' / 'levar (tempo)', 'custar (dinheiro)') entirely — those belong to 掛かる. Keep only the illness sense: en ['to catch (an illness), to come down with'], pt ['pegar (uma doença), contrair'], which becomes the single sense of 罹る.
issue: Sense belongs to the homophone 掛かる, not 罹る. The headword 罹る only means 'to suffer from / to catch (an illness)' (already covered by senses[1]). Teaching 'to take (time)/to cost (money)' under 罹る is false; the pt 'levar (tempo), custar (dinheiro)' mirrors the same error.

current: to hold (an event); to open (a show)
issue: 'To hold (an event)/to open (a show)' is a sense of the transitive reading 開く（ひらく）, not of intransitive あく (tagged vi). あく never takes an event object; this teaches a false usage (×パーティーをあく). Replace with a real あく sense, e.g. opening for business.

pt mirrors the wrong-lexeme sense: 'realizar (um evento), promover' belongs to 開く（ひらく）(transitive), not to intransitive あく. Must be replaced together with the en gloss (e.g. shop opening for business).

fix: Remove the sense-2 pt gloss ('porque; já que; pois') together with the sense. だから is 'por isso; portanto; então' only.
issue: Invented sense not in JMdict: the conjunction だから only means 'so/therefore' (it introduces a result). 'because/since (giving a reason)' is the gloss of から/ので — the causal direction is reversed, so this sense teaches another word's meaning.

fix: Remove the sense-2 pt gloss ('porque; já que; pois') together with the sense. だから is 'por isso; portanto; então' only.
issue: Mirrors the invented EN sense: 'porque/já que/pois' introduce a reason clause, which だから can never do (it introduces the consequence). A Brazilian learner would produce cause-effect-reversed sentences.

current: to get thirsty; to be parched
fix: Delete the second sense ("to get thirsty; to be parched" / pt "ficar com sede, ressecar (garganta)"). JMdict entry 1209650 乾く【かわく】 means only "to dry / to become dry" (v5k, vi); the thirst sense belongs to the separate homophone lexeme 渇く【かわく】 (のどが渇く). Keep only sense[0] "to dry; to become dry" / "secar, ficar seco".
issue: Sense 'to get thirsty; to be parched' belongs to the homophone lexeme 渇く (kawaku, thirst), not 乾く. JMdict keeps them as separate entries; 乾く means only 'to become dry'. The pt glosses 'ficar com sede, ressecar (garganta)' carry the same wrong-lexeme meaning.

'To reflect (an image); to project' are glosses of the homophone 映す (utsusu), not 写す. 写す means to copy/photograph/depict. Also, 写す's must-know core sense 'to photograph' is missing from the entry; it should replace this sense.
'Refletir (uma imagem); projetar' translates the homophone 映す, not 写す. Should carry 写す's missing core photo sense instead.

current: to pass on (a cold), to infect
issue: 'To pass on (a cold), to infect' is a gloss of the homophone 移す (utsusu, e.g. 風邪を移す), not 写す. A real remaining sense of 写す is 'to describe/depict'.
'Transmitir (resfriado), contagiar' translates the homophone 移す, not 写す. Should match the corrected EN sense (describe/depict).

current: to depart; to leave; to set off
issue: Core noun meaning 'departure' is missing. pos is [n, vs, vi] and every other suru-noun in this batch (入学, 入院, 冷房, 利用, 出席) includes the nominal gloss; 出発 gives only verbal glosses.
Missing the nominal gloss 'partida' matching the n pos; also 'ir embora' (to go away for good) drifts from 出発 (to set off/depart on a journey) and is best dropped.
Romaji 'genin' does not match the kana げんいん: it reads as げにん (ge-ni-n). Syllabic ん before a vowel requires disambiguation, e.g. gen'in. This is a kana-mismatch, not a wapuro style variant.

'To visit' is the meaning of the homophone 訪ねる (also read たずねる), a separate lexeme. 尋ねる means to ask/inquire and, secondarily, to search/look for (JMdict sense 2). Teaching 尋ねる = visit confuses the classic N4 confusable pair 尋ねる vs 訪ねる.
'visitar, ir ver' renders the homophone 訪ねる, not 尋ねる. If the EN sense is corrected to the real second sense of 尋ねる (to search/look for), the pt must follow.

current: to be (animate); to exist; to stay
fix: Add the register that distinguishes おる from いる. en: ["to be (animate; humble/courteous form of いる)", "to exist", "to stay"]; pt: ["estar (forma humilde/cortês de いる)", "ficar", "existir"]; and set misc/register to [hum] rather than null. Prefer 'humble/courteous' over a flat 'humble' since おる is also plain-condescending or dialectally neutral outside the ~おります form.
issue: おる is the humble/courteous counterpart of いる (JMdict tags it [hum]), but both en and pt gloss it as plain neutral 'to be'. Using おる neutrally (e.g. about the listener or a teacher) sounds rude or dialectal. Sibling entries like 差し上げる do mark humility in the gloss; this one should too.
Syllabic ん before a vowel needs an apostrophe: 'tenin' transliterates てにん, not てんいん. This is a reading ambiguity, not a style choice.
彼ら refers to male or mixed groups (JMdict: 'usually of males'); an all-female group is 彼女たち/彼女ら. Glossing it as 'elas' invites learners to use 彼ら for a group of women.

fix: en third gloss: "exists (polite)" (drop 'humble/polite copula'). pt third gloss 'tem (formal)' is fine; existe (forma polida) already covers the existence sense.
issue: ございます by itself is the polite existence verb (polite ある), not a copula — the copula is でございます. It is also polite (丁寧語), not humble. The parenthetical teaches wrong grammar terminology.

fix: to strike (the hour; of a clock)
issue: Garbled parenthetical: 'to strike (a clock the hour)' is not grammatical English; a word or separator is missing. Meaning (clock striking the hour) is correct but the wording needs a rewrite.

current: transmissão, programa, transmitir, ir ao ar
issue: pt gloss list includes 'programa', which is the meaning of 番組 (TV/radio program), not 放送 (the act of broadcasting / a transmission). It has no counterpart in the en glosses and blurs a distinction JLPT materials test; a learner could say 放送 when they mean 番組.

current: to be empty | to be uncrowded | to be vacant
fix: to be empty | to be uncrowded
issue: Gloss 'to be vacant' belongs to the homophone reading 空く(あく). 空く(すく) means to become less crowded/empty (電車がすく); it is not used for a vacant seat/room, which is あく. This imports the other lexeme's gloss and invites the classic あく/すく misuse.
Romaji 'honyaku' is ambiguous: syllabic n before ya requires an apostrophe, otherwise it reads as ho-nya-ku (ほにゃく), not ほんやく. Needs 'hon'yaku'.
'cumprimentar' primarily means 'to greet' in pt-BR; listed bare it suggests homeru = greet someone. For 'to compliment/commend' the natural pt-BR is 'parabenizar' or 'fazer um elogio'.

見える 'to come' is sonkeigo (honorific: the subject is a respected other), not merely polite. '(polite)'/'(cortês)' invites learners to use it for their own coming. The batch's own convention marks keigo category precisely (致す = 'to do (humble)').

fix: Remove the second sense ('counter for houses' / pt 'contador de casas') entirely. For hw 軒 + kana のき the word means only 'eaves (of a roof)'. The counter-for-houses meaning belongs to a separate lexeme, 軒 read けん (ken), and must not appear under the のき entry.
issue: Sense 'counter for houses' belongs to a different lexeme: 軒 read けん (ken). For this hw+kana pair (軒/のき) the word means only 'eaves'. The pt 'contador de casas' repeats the same error.

current: to be known as, to pass as
fix: Replace sense 2 with en: ['to circulate (of blood)','to be conveyed (of feelings)'] / pt: ['circular (o sangue)','ser transmitido (sentimentos)']. The 'known as / pass as' meaning belongs to 通る (vocab:1433030), not 通う.
issue: Sense 2 glosses 'to be known as / to pass as' belong to 通る (とおる), not 通う (e.g. 天才で通っている). 通う's actual secondary senses are 'to be conveyed (of feelings)' / 'to circulate (of blood)'. The pt list ('ser conhecido como', 'passar por') mirrors the same wrong sense.
'correr' alone means 'to run' (= 走る), not 'to run away'; listing it as a gloss of 逃げる invites the learner to confuse the two verbs. The EN list correctly has no plain 'to run'.
'atrapalho' is not a standard noun in Brazilian Portuguese (the derived noun is 'atrapalhação'); it reads as an improvised form in a dictionary gloss.

Gloss 'sem jeito' in pt-BR primarily means 'awkward/embarrassed' (ficar sem jeito) or 'clumsy', not 'no good/useless/hopeless'. The intended idiom is 'não tem jeito'; as a bare gloss it suggests a wrong meaning for だめ.
In the 'far (away) / way (off)' sense, bare "muito" does not render distance (it duplicates sense 2's intensifier meaning), and "bem mais longe" adds a comparative 'mais' not present in the sense.

Romaji 'bonyari' is ambiguous for ぼんやり: without a separator it reads as bo-nya-ri (ぼにゃり). Syllabic ん before や requires an apostrophe (Hepburn bon'yari) or doubled n in wapuro; as written it does not round-trip to the kana.

fix: Replace senses[2].en with: ["just keeps (doing/getting)", "only continues to", "increasingly (in one direction)"]
issue: Gloss 'the more ... (the more ...)' describes the correlative 〜ば〜ほど construction, not 一方(だ), which marks a trend that just keeps going in one direction (悪化する一方だ = 'just keeps getting worse'). Misleading for a core N3 grammar use; could teach learners to use 一方 in 'the more X, the more Y' sentences.

fix: Replace senses[0].pt with: ["geral", "comum", "normal"] (drop 'ordinário'; 'corriqueiro' is also acceptable in place of 'normal')
issue: In Brazilian Portuguese 'ordinário' is read by default as pejorative (shoddy, vulgar, despicable person); as a bare gloss for 一般 'general/common' it invites embarrassing misuse (e.g. 'uma família ordinária'). Register trap for pt-BR learners.

'algures' is European Portuguese vocabulary. It is archaic/literary and virtually unused in everyday Brazilian Portuguese, where 'em algum lugar' (already given) is standard. Inappropriate to teach in a pt-BR course.

For 印刷 'printing/print', gloss 'imprensa' is a false friend: in Brazilian Portuguese 'imprensa' means the press/news media (or the printing-press machine), not the act/result of printing. Correct term 'impressão' is already present.
'apoiante' is the European Portuguese form for 'supporter'; Brazilian Portuguese standardly uses 'apoiador'.

fix: delete this sense: 実(み) means fruit/nut/seed/content, not 'truth' (that is 実 じつ)
issue: For 実 read み, JMdict lists only fruit/nut; seed; broth ingredients; content/substance. 'truth/reality' is the じつ reading's meaning, not み. This sense assigns another reading's gloss to this lexeme (teaches something false). Same defect in senses[0].pt.

current: en: 'degree (of temperature, angle)' / pt: 'grau (de temperatura, ângulo)'
fix: Remove this sense — 'degree' is the ど reading; 度/たび = time/occasion only.
issue: The 'degree (of temperature, angle)' sense belongs to the reading ど, not to たび. For hw 度 + kana たび, the lexeme means only time/occasion/counter-of-times. Teaching that たび means 'degree' is a false meaning (wrong reading imported). Affects both en and pt of sense 3.

fix: (remove — 'pattern/design' is 柄 がら, not え; え = handle only)
issue: 柄 read え means only 'handle/haft'. The 'pattern, design (on cloth)' sense (en+pt 'estampa, padrão') belongs to the がら reading (entry 1508300, listed as the next item), not え. Teaches a false meaning for this lexeme.

current: nature, character (of a person) / índole, natureza
fix: (remove — 'nature/character' is 柄 がら, not え; え = handle only)
issue: 柄 read え means only 'handle/haft'. The 'nature, character (of a person)' sense (en+pt 'índole, natureza') belongs to the がら reading, not え. Teaches a false meaning for this lexeme.

current: tag, label, card / etiqueta, ficha, placa
fix: (remove — 'tag/label/card' is 札 ふだ, not さつ)
issue: 札 read さつ means only 'banknote/bill'. The 'tag, label, card' sense (en+pt 'etiqueta, ficha, placa') belongs to the ふだ reading (separate JMdict entry), not さつ. Teaches a false meaning for this lexeme.

fix: Remove this sense entirely (heatstroke = 熱中症, not 熱中).
issue: 熱中 (ねっちゅう) does not mean 'heatstroke'. It only means being absorbed/engrossed/enthusiastic. Heatstroke is 熱中症 (ねっちゅうしょう). This entire second sense (EN 'heatstroke'; PT 'insolação, intermação') is a fabricated meaning from confusing 熱中 with 熱中症 — teaches a false meaning.

current: even though / in spite of (the fact that)
fix: Replace sense 2 with the JMdict noun sense en:['kink','crease','curl'] / pt:['cacho','dobra','vinco'], or remove it entirely.
issue: The concessive meaning 'even though / in spite of' belongs to the fixed particle/conjunction くせに, not to the bare noun 癖 (くせ), whose senses are habit/quirk/tendency and kink/crease/curl. Glossing a noun sense as 'even though' is misleading.

fix: rutting, being in heat (of animals); mating season
issue: For the reading さかり (sakari), 盛り means peak/height/prime (and secondarily 'in heat/rutting season' for animals). The glosses 'heap, serving' belong to the OTHER reading もり (mori), as in 大盛り/山盛り. さかり does not mean a serving or heap, so this sense misattributes another reading's meaning to this lexeme. The pt 'porção (servida), monte' inherits the same error.

fix: Remove this sense — belongs to しゅ/種類, not たね; たね = 'seed, pip' (already covered by sense[1]).
issue: 種 read as たね means 'seed' (correctly in sense[1]); it does NOT mean 'kind/type/sort'. That is the しゅ reading / 種類 (しゅるい) — the adjacent entry in this batch. Sense[0] en ('kind, type, sort') and pt ('tipo, espécie') teach a false meaning via cross-entry contamination.

For the physical chain 鎖 (EN 'chain'), the second pt gloss 'cadeia' is misleading in pt-BR, where 'cadeia' reads first as 'jail/prison'; a metal chain is 'corrente'. 'cadeia' also doesn't fit the figurative bond sense (that'd be 'grilhões').
銃 is a generic 'gun/firearm' (EN has no 'rifle'). The pt gloss 'fuzil' means specifically 'rifle', narrowing the generic term and adding a meaning absent from the EN set.

current: senses[1]: en [edge, verge, brink]; pt [beira, borda]
fix: Remove this sense — it is the 際【きわ】 lexeme; 際【さい】 only means occasion/time.
issue: Sense 2 (en 'edge/verge/brink'; pt 'beira, borda') is misattributed. 際 read さい means only occasion/time/circumstances/when (JMdict 1296300). The edge/verge/brink meaning belongs to the separate lexeme 際【きわ】 (JMdict 1296290). This teaches a false meaning for さい.

fix: Remove this sense entirely — 額(がく) = 'quantia/montante' and 'moldura' only; 'testa/forehead' is the ひたい reading.
issue: The がく reading of 額 does not mean 'forehead'. Raw JMdict entry 1207500 has only two senses: framed picture/frame and amount/sum. 'Forehead' belongs to the ひたい reading (vocab:1207510, item 9). This sense is another lexeme's gloss attached to がく and teaches a false meaning (額 as がく never means testa).

Missing accents (spelling errors): 'cardapio' should be 'cardápio' and 'refeicao' should be 'refeição'. Other entries in the batch use accents correctly, so this is an inconsistent typo, not a deliberate ASCII choice.

current: por enquanto, por ora, por hora
fix: por enquanto, por ora (remover 'por hora' = 'per hour')
issue: pt gloss list for ひとまず ('for now / for the time being') includes 'por hora', which in Brazilian Portuguese means 'per hour' (a rate), not 'for now'. The correct form 'por ora' is already listed. 'por hora' teaches a false meaning.

'rouge' is a false friend in Brazilian Portuguese: it means cheek blush, not lipstick. 口紅 is specifically lipstick and never means blush, so this teaches a wrong secondary meaning. 'batom' already covers the word fully.
Kana あんい has three morae (a-n-i) with ん before a vowel. The romaji 'ani' does not disambiguate ん and reads back as あに (兄). It should carry an apostrophe: 'an'i'.
Pleonastic/awkward rendering of 'flatland': 'planície plana' is redundant since 'planície' already denotes flat terrain. A reviewer would fix it.

Under the current Brazilian orthographic norm (Acordo Ortográfico), the prefix 'auto-' joins directly before a different vowel (cf. autoescola, autoavaliação). 'estudo' begins with 'e', so the correct spelling is 'autoestudo', not the hyphenated 'auto-estudo'.

fix: Remove this sense — 課程 = course/curriculum only; 'process/stages' belongs to homophone 過程
issue: Second sense 'process / stages' (processo / etapas) is not a meaning of 課程. It is the meaning of the homophone 過程 (かてい). 課程 means only 'course of study / curriculum'. This glosses a different lexeme's meaning onto this headword.
The counter 通 (つう) counts letters, notes and documents/emails, not phone calls (those use 本 or 件). 'phone calls' is inaccurate; same error in the pt gloss ('telefonemas').
'a passear' is a European Portuguese progressive construction (a + infinitive). Brazilian Portuguese uses the gerund; a pt-BR reviewer would write 'passeando' (or 'vagando').

'saldo' as a word for a retail sale is European Portuguese. In pt-BR 'saldo' means an account balance; Brazilian clearance/sale is 'liquidação', 'promoção', or 'queima de estoque'. Teaching 'saldo' = sale would mislead a Brazilian learner.

ビジネス means 'business/commerce' (the activity), not 'empresa' (company/firm = 会社/企業). The EN glosses are 'business, commerce' with no 'company', so 'empresa' is an imprecise/misleading extra gloss; 'negócios' already carries the core sense.

fix: long (time since); (it has been) a long time; long-lasting
issue: 久しい means 'a long time has passed / long-lasting'; it does not carry the anticipation nuance of 'long-overdue' or 'long-awaited' (that is 待ち遠しい/待ちに待った). These two glosses teach a false nuance.

"recolha" is European Portuguese for 'collection'; Brazilian Portuguese uses "coleta" (and it is redundant with the correct "recolhimento" already in the list). Not a meaning error, but a pt-PT regionalism a pt-BR reviewer would replace.

fix: (remove sense 2 — illness-chills belongs to 寒気/さむけ, not かんき)
issue: 寒気/かんき means only cold / cold air / cold weather. The second sense 'chills (from illness), shivers' belongs to the separate reading さむけ (present as the adjacent entry vocab:1210410). JMdict split 2866134 exists precisely to keep かんき (cold) apart from さむけ (illness chills); attributing the illness sense to かんき conflates the two lexemes.

対談 is a two-way conversation/talk between two people, not an interview. The pt gloss 'entrevista' (= interview) mistranslates the EN 'talk (between two people)' and introduces an interviewer/interviewee meaning the word does not carry; the correct senses (conversa, diálogo) are already present.

'cursada' as a noun is not natural Brazilian Portuguese (it is a Spanish/River Plate construction, e.g. 'la cursada'). A pt-BR reviewer would rephrase; the meaning of 必修 (compulsory subject) is already carried by the first gloss.

current: en: bill, banknote / pt: nota (dinheiro), cédula
fix: Remove this sense (banknote is 札 read さつ, not ふだ)
issue: The 'bill, banknote' sense is restricted to the reading さつ (e.g. お札=おさつ), not ふだ. For the ふだ lexeme this reading-restricted sense is wrong; ふだ means tag/label/ticket/charm, not paper money. Teaching ふだ='banknote' mis-associates the reading.

False friend. EN 'mimicry' here means imitation/copying (模倣 = imitação/cópia), but pt-BR 'mímica' means the art of mime/gesture (fazer mímica = charades), not imitation. Should be 'mimetismo' or dropped; the first two glosses already cover the sense.

European Portuguese construction 'a ferver' (estar a + infinitive) used instead of Brazilian gerund. The pt list already contains the Brazilian form 'água fervendo', making the pt-PT 'água a ferver' a clear locale violation. 'escaldante' alone is fine and covers 'scalding hot water'.

In pt-BR, 'previdência social' specifically denotes the contributory pension/social-security (INSS) system, not welfare. 福祉 = welfare/well-being (bem-estar, assistência social). This third gloss introduces a concept absent from the EN set ('welfare, well-being, social welfare') and inaccurate to the lexeme.

current: en: to regulate, to control, to restrict | pt: regular, controlar, restringir
fix: Add a noun sense FIRST (before the verb sense): en 'regulation, control, restriction' / pt 'regulamentação, controle, restrição'; keep the existing verb sense second.
issue: 規制 is predominantly used as a noun meaning 'regulation, control, restriction' (e.g. 規制緩和 = deregulation, 交通規制 = traffic control), yet the only sense glosses it solely as a verb. The must-know noun core sense is missing, unlike every other suru-noun in this batch (規定, 要望, 要請 all split a noun sense).

fix: to be cleared up (of tension, a misunderstanding); to dissolve
issue: 'to be solved (problem)' is a gloss of the homograph reading とける, not ほどける. 問題が解ける ('solve a problem') is read とける. ほどける means only 'to come undone' and figuratively 'to be cleared up / dissolve' (tension, a misunderstanding, e.g. わだかまりがほどける), never solving a problem.
Mirror of the EN error: 'ser resolvido (problema)' renders a とける meaning. For ほどける the figurative sense is a tension/misunderstanding coming undone, not a problem being solved.

'corno' as a plain synonym for animal horn is a register landmine in pt-BR: it overwhelmingly reads as the slang insult for a cuckold. 'chifre' and 'galhada' already cover the sense; 'corno' should be dropped for a learner dictionary.

fix: Remove the 'levar de cangaru' gloss; keep pt as ["carregar nas costas (esp. uma criança)", "cavalinho (carregar nas costas)"]
issue: Spelling error: 'cangaru' should be 'canguru' (kangaroo). Also a weak rendering of おんぶ (back-carrying), since 'canguru/bebê canguru' in pt-BR connotes front-of-chest carrying; the sense is already covered by the other two glosses.

False friend: EN 'declining (politely)' means polite refusal, but Portuguese noun 'declínio' means decline/decay/downfall, never refusal. Teaches a false meaning for 辞退. (Note the verb 'declinar' in sense 2 is correct; only the noun 'declínio' here is wrong.)
鉄鋼 (てっこう) means the material 'iron and steel'. 'siderurgia' denotes the steel-making industry/process, not the material, so it does not align with the EN gloss 'iron and steel'.
